Growth Courant numbers on the consumer size grid

Source: R/transport.R
getCourant.Rd

Measures how far growth can transport fish through a size bin during dt. Each value is dt / dw times the larger positive growth velocity at the bin's inflow and outflow faces. The face convention follows the configured flux scheme: upwind uses g[j - 1] and g[j], whereas the second-order schemes use g[j] and g[j + 1]. Recruitment replaces growth inflow at the egg boundary. Values outside the species' retained size support are zero; empty but reachable bins are included.

Usage

getCourant(
  params,
  dt = 1,
  n = initialN(params),
  n_pp = initialNResource(params),
  n_other = initialNOther(params),
  effort = params@initial_effort,
  t = 0,
  e_growth = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

params

A MizerParams object.

dt

Positive time interval in years. Default 1 gives the Courant number per year, which scales linearly with the chosen interval.

n

Consumer number densities. Defaults to the initial state.

n_pp

Resource number densities. Defaults to the initial state.

n_other

Other component abundances. Defaults to the initial state.

effort

Fishing effort, as in getRates().

t

Time at which to calculate the rates, in years.

e_growth

Optional precomputed growth matrix, with the same dimensions and, when present, species and size labels as initialN(params). Must be finite. If omitted, growth is obtained from getRates() at the supplied state, respecting custom rate functions.

...

Further arguments passed to the rate functions.

Value

An ArraySpeciesBySize containing dimensionless growth Courant numbers. With no positive growth every entry is zero.

Details

A large value can indicate cell-scale oscillations with a high-order flux. The target used by project() is an advisory growth-based measure, not a universal stability or positivity bound. It does not measure mortality, diffusion or changes in rates during the step. The exact bin widths are used, not the approximation w * log(w[2] / w[1]).

Examples

max(getCourant(NS_params, dt = 1 / 52))
#> [1] 12.70361
